headline: The January company-wide fall is the December-to-January seasonal reset, not a deterioration.

evidence.what: Company net revenue peaks every December and troughs every January in both years
evidence.figures: Dec-2024 EUR15,965,841 (annual high) -> Jan-2025 EUR11,383,322 (MoM -28.7%); Jan-2024 EUR11,098,719 was likewise 2024's low month; Dec-2025 EUR17,287,265

evidence.what: Same-month year-on-year growth for January is positive and healthy
evidence.figures: Jan-2025 net revenue YoY +2.6% (EUR11,383,322 vs EUR11,098,719)

recommended_action: Report January against the prior January, not against December; drop the month-on-month flag on the seasonal turn.

headline: The Nordics material-cost flag is a volume artifact: unit material cost is flat to down and on budget, so it is not a cost problem.

evidence.what: Material cost per unit is flat in every BU x line (largest move under 0.5%); Nordics fell
evidence.figures: Nordics material/unit 2024 EUR1.3143 -> 2025 EUR1.2952 (-1.5%); Nordics Home Care EUR1.1700 -> EUR1.1733; Nordics volume 20.6m -> 23.3m units (+13%), which fully explains the euro rise

evidence.what: Actual unit material cost is at or below budget
evidence.figures: Nordics 2025 actual EUR1.2952/unit vs budget EUR1.3052; Central Europe EUR1.3162 vs EUR1.3052; Baltics & Poland EUR1.3103 vs EUR1.3052

evidence.what: PVM confirms material-cost price (unit) effect is negligible; the change is volume
evidence.figures: Company material cost delta +EUR6,574,281 = volume +EUR7,073,049, mix -EUR530,979, price +EUR32,211

recommended_action: Reframe the material-cost flags as volume-driven; the margin question they are mistaken for is addressed under F3 and F8.

headline: The recurring EBITDA-vs-budget miss is a margin problem from a step-up in promotional discounting, not cost or volume; underlying EBITDA is EUR5.6m below budget.
claimed_cause: Promotional discount rates were stepped up sharply from February 2025 (Nordics 5.9% to ~10%; Baltics & Poland 8% climbing to 17%), cutting net price per unit while material, labour and volume tracked plan; the discount give-away more than accounts for the entire EBITDA shortfall.

evidence.what: Company discount rate (promo/gross) roughly doubled through 2025, starting February; company gross margin broke at the same month
evidence.figures: discount rate 5.8% (Jan-25) -> 8.4% (Feb-25) -> 10.4% (Dec-25) vs a steady ~5.9% across all of 2024; company gross margin 42.3% (Jan-25) -> ~40.0% from Feb-25

evidence.what: Extra discount in 2025 vs holding each BU's 2024 discount rate
evidence.figures: Company EUR5,862,440 (Nordics EUR3,632,687; Baltics & Poland EUR2,258,321; Central Europe -EUR28,568)

evidence.what: Underlying EBITDA miss vs budget decomposes to margin, not cost or opex at company level
evidence.figures: FY2025 underlying EBITDA EUR15,497,896 vs budget EUR21,134,482 = -EUR5,636,586; gross-profit miss -EUR3,259,058, S&M over +EUR1,416,393, admin over +EUR961,135; net revenue actually beat budget by +EUR5,992,231

evidence.what: Company EBITDA vs budget steps from a ~9% miss to a ~28% miss exactly at February 2025
evidence.figures: 2024 miss 2.7% to 12.6% per month; underlying miss 27.5% (Feb-25), 28.9% (Mar), 29.1% (May) ... 31.5% (Nov), 29.9% (Dec)

recommended_action: Put the discount/net-price policy on the board agenda: quantify the return on the incremental EUR5.9m of promotional spend and set a net-price floor by line and BU.

headline: The Baltics & Poland net-revenue flags are genuine volume growth, not a data or one-off distortion.

evidence.what: Baltics & Poland revenue growth is carried by real unit volume, not price
PVM attributes the B&P revenue gain to volume, offset by price
evidence.figures: B&P net revenue delta +EUR8,389,592 = volume +EUR10,177,682, mix -EUR137,818, price -EUR1,650,272

recommended_action: Treat the B&P top-line flags as expected growth; the concern is its economics, covered under F5.

headline: Baltics & Poland growth is uneconomic: revenue rose 27% but underlying EBITDA fell 8%, on deeper discounting plus S&M and admin overspend.
claimed_cause: The volume was bought with an escalating discount (8% to 17% of gross through the year) and with sales & marketing and admin spend well above budget, so a 27% revenue gain produced an EBITDA decline.

evidence.what: B&P underlying EBITDA fell year-on-year despite the revenue surge
evidence.figures: underlying EBITDA EUR3,209,582 (2024) -> EUR2,949,511 (2025), -8.1%; gross margin 41.4% -> 38.5%; discount rate rising to 17.1% by Dec-2025

evidence.what: B&P opex ran well over budget

recommended_action: Review whether the Baltics & Poland volume is worth its cost; hold S&M and admin to budget and test a lower discount level for margin recovery.

headline: The Central Europe DSO deterioration is one customer, Rheinkauf Gruppe, whose overdue balance has more than doubled while its collections fell.
claimed_cause: Rheinkauf Gruppe, Central Europe's largest account (45-day terms), stopped paying to terms: its closing receivable built from EUR2.06m to EUR4.49m through 2025 (about four months of its own sales outstanding), while every other CE account stayed near two months and on terms.

evidence.what: Rheinkauf closing AR versus all other CE customers
evidence.figures: Rheinkauf EUR2,060,367 (Dec-2024) -> EUR4,493,177 (Dec-2025), +EUR2,432,809; next-largest CE mover Delta Benelux +EUR165,286; all others +/-EUR165k or less

evidence.what: Rheinkauf receivable expressed in months of its own revenue, against contractual terms
evidence.figures: Dec-2025 AR EUR4,493,177 vs avg monthly net revenue EUR1,175,762 = ~4.0 months outstanding against 45-day (~1.5 month) terms

evidence.what: Rheinkauf collections fell year-on-year even as its sales grew

recommended_action: Escalate the Rheinkauf overdue balance to collection and a credit-limit review; it is concentration and credit risk, not a general CE trend.

headline: The April EBITDA spike is a EUR2.2m one-off other-income item in Nordics; underlying April was in line with the year's shortfall.

evidence.what: Other income is zero every month except April 2025, and sits entirely in Nordics
evidence.figures: Nordics other income EUR2,200,000 in Apr-2025; EUR0 in all other months and all other BUs; budget other income EUR0

evidence.what: Stripping the one-off, April operating EBITDA matches the rest of 2025
evidence.figures: reported EBITDA EUR3,394,941 (+196% MoM) vs underlying EUR1,194,941; underlying April was -28.1% vs budget, the same band as Feb-Dec

evidence.what: A EUR5.5m investing inflow lands in the same month, consistent with a one-off asset disposal (gain in other income, proceeds in investing cash flow)
evidence.figures: investing cash flow EUR5,500,000 in Apr-2025; EUR0 in every other month

recommended_action: Label the April figure as a non-recurring gain in the pack so it is not read as operating improvement or extrapolated.

headline: The pack's BU grain hides that Home Care is the epicentre: the lowest-margin line is discounted hardest and is gaining volume share, a double margin drag.
claimed_cause: Home Care, the lowest-margin line, took the bulk of the discount escalation (Nordics Home Care jumped from 6.0% to 18.8% of gross in a single month, Feb 2025) and grew its share of volume, so mix and price move against margin together.

evidence.what: Home Care margin, discount and volume share, 2024 vs 2025 (company)
evidence.figures: Home Care gross margin 27.6% -> 20.8%; discount rate 5.9% -> 14.7%; volume share 36.3% -> 41.3%; other lines' margins roughly stable (Hair ~45%, Skin & Body ~47%)

evidence.what: Home Care share of the extra 2025 discount vs 2024 line rates
evidence.figures: Home Care EUR4,168,547 of the company's EUR5,862,440 extra discount (71%); Skin & Body EUR773,671, Hair Care EUR640,563, Professional EUR490,822

evidence.what: Nordics Home Care discount is a February step-change, not a drift
evidence.figures: Nordics Home Care discount rate 6.0% (Jan-25) -> 18.8% (Feb-25), holding ~19-20% for the rest of the year

recommended_action: Add a product-line margin view to the pack and target the Home Care discount and mix directly, since it drives the bulk of the shortfall.

headline: Part of the EBITDA-vs-budget gap is chronic budget optimism: EBITDA missed budget by ~8% in 2024 too, before any discounting.
claimed_cause: The 2024 budget was already set above delivered margin, so about a third of the 2025 vs-budget EBITDA gap predates the discount action and reflects a standing planning bias rather than a new operational event.

evidence.what: FY2024 EBITDA missed budget across the board, with no discounting present
evidence.figures: FY2024 EBITDA EUR17,956,325 vs budget EUR19,562,535 = -8.2%; every month of 2024 missed by 2.7% to 12.6%; 2024 discount rate flat at ~5.9%

recommended_action: Separate the standing ~8% budget bias from the ~20-point discount-driven gap when the board judges 2025 performance, and recalibrate the 2026 margin assumption.

headline: Operating cash generation fell EUR3.4m year-on-year as receivables absorbed cash; healthy closing cash is flattered by the EUR5.5m April one-off.
claimed_cause: Weaker underlying EBITDA and a EUR3.9m build in receivables (Rheinkauf being the largest single piece) cut operating cash flow; the year's cash increase leans on the non-recurring EUR5.5m investing inflow.

evidence.what: Operating cash flow down year-on-year; closing cash increase partly one-off
evidence.figures: operating CF EUR13,690,781 (2024) -> EUR10,296,273 (2025), -EUR3,394,508; closing cash EUR21,690,781 -> EUR37,487,053, of which EUR5,500,000 is April investing inflow

evidence.what: Company receivables built through 2025, tying up cash
evidence.figures: closing receivables EUR17,670,729 (Dec-2024) -> EUR21,532,773 (Dec-2025), +EUR3,862,044

recommended_action: Track operating cash conversion (excluding one-offs) alongside EBITDA, and recover the Rheinkauf balance to release working capital.
